prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production animation sprite sheet for a tiny desktop music companion. Single subject: CHARACTER. Cute super-deformed chibi, large head and tiny body, refined hand-painted game illustration, clean silhouettes, soft shaded volume, expressive face, detailed recognizable costume, readable at 120 pixels. One character only, repeated EXACTLY 24 times in a precise uniform FOUR COLUMNS by SIX ROWS grid on a truly TRANSPARENT background, no guides, no borders, no text, no labels, no ground, no cast shadows. Portrait sheet aspect 2:3. Every tile square. Character fills about 75% of its tile, horizontally centered, feet baseline at 90% tile height, generous empty gaps, no figure overlaps another tile. Same scale, face and outfit across all cells.
Ordered left-to-right, top-to-bottom:
Tiles 1-8 (rows 1-2): a complete gentle listening groove LOOP: neutral, lean slightly left, left downbeat with knees bent, recover left, neutral, lean slightly right, right downbeat, recover right. Arms naturally follow. Eyes open.
Tiles 9-16 (rows 3-4): a complete cheerful dancing LOOP: neutral, step left with left arm raised, soft bend both knees, return center, neutral, step right with right arm raised, soft bend both knees, return center. Characters with no arms move only their real limbs. Keep accessories stable.
Tiles 17-20 (row 5): relaxed standing eyes open; same standing eyes closed blink; peaceful sleeping eyes closed; friendly hello wave (or head tilt for armless subject).
Tiles 21-24 (row 6): being picked up with surprised face and dangling legs; relaxed dangling with open eyes; little landing crouch with eyes briefly closed; recovered relaxed standing.
No added humans or objects holding the character. Anatomically consistent, no extra limbs, no detached hands, no body redesign. Preserve exact iconic palette. Draw each complete figure fully within its own tile.
